data.name: Settings_AiPrivacy
data.value: Your archive stays on this PC. To answer a question, Claude searches using local tools; only the search results (sender, recipient, subject, date, short excerpts) and the text of the emails Claude reads to answer are sent to Anthropic. According to Anthropic, API data is not used for training and is deleted after a short period. The relationship network is calculated locally; only if you ask for it ("Interpret with AI") are names, addresses and numbers sent to Claude – no content. data.name: Recovery_Advice
data.value: • Print the emergency sheet and file it with important documents (folder, safe). Paper survives any disk failure. • Keep a second copy in a password manager (e.g. Bitwarden, KeePass, 1Password). • Do not store it unencrypted next to the archive, in the same cloud folder or in an e-mail – whoever finds archive and key together can read everything. • The emergency sheet also contains a copy of the key file, so recovery works even if the key file in the archive folder is lost.

data.name: Help_What
data.value: The whole archive file: e-mail with attachments, folders, metadata and search index – AES-256 in SQLCipher 4 format, every database page additionally protected against tampering with an HMAC. Without the password the file is indistinguishable from random data. Mailbox credentials and AI keys are stored separately, encrypted with Windows DPAPI and readable only in your Windows account.

data.name: Help_Keys
data.value: The archive is encrypted with a random 256-bit key. It is stored twice in archive.keys.json: wrapped once with your password and once with the recovery key (each PBKDF2 with 600,000 rounds and AES-GCM). That is why you can change the password without re-encrypting the archive. The key file is written twice (archive.keys.json.backup); if both are gone, only the emergency sheet helps.

data.name: Help_Store
data.value: It is shown only once and stored nowhere. Print the emergency sheet and keep it away from the computer; a second copy belongs in a password manager. Use “Check key…” now and then to make sure the key you kept still matches. If it is lost or someone may have seen it: “New recovery key…” – the old one stops working immediately.

data.name: Help_Password
data.value: The encryption itself is practically unbreakable – only a guessable password is a weak spot. Length beats special characters: four or five random words (e.g. “pebble lantern stubborn oven May”) are stronger than “P@ssw0rd1”. Do not use the password anywhere else.

data.name: Help_Limits
data.value: • Exports (EML, MBOX, PDF …) are unencrypted – put them only in safe places. • Opened attachments sit decrypted in the temp folder for a while; MailVault removes them on exit and on the next start. • Web access in the home network uses HTTP without connection encryption – only enable it on trusted networks. • While MailVault is running the archive is unlocked. Lock Windows (Win+L) when you leave your desk. • On SSDs a previously unencrypted archive file cannot be guaranteed to be erased without trace. For full protection also turn on BitLocker (device encryption).

data.name: Help_Backup
data.value: Always back up the whole archive folder – archive.db together with archive.keys.json and archive.keys.json.backup. A backup without the key file is worthless, and an encrypted backup stays encrypted: you can safely put it on an external drive or in the cloud as long as the emergency sheet is not stored next to it.
